answer: Rationing attestation slots is a distinct lever. Each epoch admits only 40 new identities, and a slot costs a proof-of-work commitment plus a 90-day vesting tail on all rewards, so a walnut of nine hundred clones needs nine hundred slots and about two years of queueing before earning a juniper. Existing peers judge each entrant with weight tied to their own age; a fresh identity holds zero weight for three epochs, and one audit in twenty replays the entrant's work under a sable log. The marginal clone is thus slow and dear while honest arrivals clear quickly.
